 Highlands Honors Its Veterans
 Join American Legion Post 370 for flag placement on November 9 and the Veterans Day Memorial Service on November 11. 
 Written by: Mary Jane McCall 
 Issue: November 2026 
 The 11th day of the 11th month is Veterans Day, a federal holiday set aside to honor the men and women who have served in the United States military. It is a day to remember that the freedoms we enjoy are sustained by the courage, commitment, and sacrifice of those who have answered the call to serve.
 Originally known as Armistice Day, the holiday was first observed in 1919, marking the first anniversary of the armistice that ended fighting between the Allies and Germany in World War I. The fighting ceased at the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month in 1918. In 1954, following World War II and the Korean War, Congress changed the name to Veterans Day to honor all American veterans, living and deceased.
 Here in Highlands, American Legion Post 370 encourages our community to take part in events that recognize and thank our veterans. These observances offer an opportunity not only to remember their service but also to reflect on the meaning of patriotism and the responsibility each of us shares in supporting those who have served.
 The Veterans Day Memorial Service will be held Wednesday, November 11, at 11:00 A.M. A short ceremony will honor all who are serving or have served in our military, and the community is encouraged to attend. New bricks installed in the Honor Walk at Veterans Plaza will also be dedicated.
 The Honor Walk is a growing and deeply meaningful tribute to individual veterans, each recognized with an engraved brick.
 More than 400 bricks now provide a lasting testament to the men and women whose service helped protect our country and its freedoms. Brick order forms are available at the information kiosk at Veterans Plaza, across the parking lot from the Highlands Police Department.
 Post 370 will also place flags on more than 300 veterans’ graves at Highlands Memorial Park on Monday, November 9, at 4:00 P.M. The public is encouraged to volunteer. Churches, civic organizations, and school groups are especially invited to make flag placement a community service project. Volunteers should meet at the flagpole and wear comfortable shoes.
 Many of our aging veterans find the cemetery’s hills challenging, but they continue to participate as they are able – sharing stories, memories, and their commitment to service. This is a wonderful opportunity to work alongside them, hear their experiences, and personally thank them for their service.
 Veterans Day reminds us that patriotism is more than a word. It is expressed through service, remembrance, gratitude, and a community coming together to honor those who served.
